commits.title: Query budget: the idle tick, the minute routes, the daily route and a cold frame are counted, with one store

changes.how: The script rewrites src/server/ratchet.baseline.json from ratchetCounts() alone. Make it carry over every top-level key of the old file that ratchetCounts() does not return: write JSON.stringify({ ...before, ...now }, null, 2) where 'before' is the parsed old file (or {} when there is none). This keeps the key queryBudget, which the integration test writes, and the keys later steps add.

Test support (the name ends in test-support.ts, so the ratchet does not count it). Export measure(run): it reads rowsRead() before, runs 'run' inside countStatements() from '@/db/statement-count', waits for the statistics to settle and reads rowsRead() again; it returns { statements: count, rowsRead: after minus before, records }. rowsRead() is: select pg_stat_clear_snapshot(); then select coalesce(sum(seq_tup_read + idx_tup_fetch), 0)::bigint from pg_stat_user_tables where schemaname = 'commerce'. Postgres writes a backend's counters out up to a second after its statement, and an idle backend's up to ten seconds after: so after 'run', read the sum once a second until two reads in a row are equal, at most 15 seconds. Use a second, dedicated 'postgres' connection for these reads (as test/integration-setup.ts opens one), so the reads are not in the count. Export idleClock(): a Date at 10:23 UTC on a Wednesday, off the hour and not seven in Oslo, for jobs that take 'now'. Export readBaseline() and writeBaseline(next): they read and write the key queryBudget of src/server/ratchet.baseline.json and leave every other key of the file as it is.

Top of file: vi.mock("next/server", () => ({ connection: async () => {}, after: () => {} })) and the next/headers mock of src/server/webhook-topics.int.test.ts line 17; set process.env.CRON_SECRET = 'query-budget' before importing a route. Each test gets a 120 second timeout. Part A, the idle tick: for each key of DISPATCHER_JOBS, run the job once outside the measure (it warms caches and lets a first run do its catch-up), then measure(() => job()); record { statements, rowsRead } under 'dispatcher.<kebab of key>' (kebab from src/server/cron-runs.ts). A job that throws is a failure of the test with the job's name. Part B, the minute routes: import the POST export of each of src/app/api/cron/{autopilot,broadcasts,cookie-scan,dream-factory,integrations,pack-pictures,page-jobs,page-looks,theme-shots}/route.ts and call it with new Request('http://localhost/api/cron/<name>', { method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: 'Bearer query-budget' }, body: '{}' }); assert the answer's status is 200, then measure a second call; record under 'route.<name>'. Part C, the daily routes: the same for subscription-reminders and usage, recorded under 'route.subscription-reminders' and 'route.usage'. Part D, a cold frame: measure the reads a first request for a store page makes before any page content: getStore('demo'), resolveShop('demo', 'no') from src/server/shop.ts, and the readers that src/app/s/[store]/[market]/layout.tsx awaits (open that file and call the same functions with the demo store, in the same order); and Kaizena Flow's frame: getPlatformChrome() from src/server/platform-navigation.ts, siteCookies() from src/server/site-cookies.ts and the readers that src/app/(platform)/layout.tsx awaits. Record as 'frame.store' and 'frame.platform'. Under vitest a 'use cache' function runs as a plain function, so each call is a cold read. Comparison: every figure is compared to queryBudget.one[<name>] in the baseline. Higher fails with the job's name, both numbers and the statements that are new (diff the records' texts against none: print the ten most repeated texts). Lower fails with 'run UPDATE_BASELINE=1 pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mts src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts'. With UPDATE_BASELINE=1 the test writes the measured figures and passes; it refuses to raise a figure unless FIRST=1 is also set. Last, a case that lists what the seed has switched on (see the next commit) so the file says what it counts. The figures are only comparable on a freshly seeded database (jobs that scan every store read more rows, and some send more statements, when other test files have left stores and orders behind), so CI runs this file alone on the fresh database (the ci.yml change below) and the sharded run leaves it out. Put this in the file's doc comment: 'Run on a freshly seeded database (node scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed): CI runs it before the other integration files.'

Never by hand: run FIRST=1 UPDATE_BASELINE=1 pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mts src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts on a freshly seeded database (node scripts/db-setup.mjs --seed on an empty DATABASE_URL). It adds the key queryBudget: { one: { '<job>': { statements, rowsRead } } }.

In the integration job (the one with `matrix: shard: [1, 2, 3]`), directly after the step 'Create the database with the demo catalogue' and before 'Integration tests against the database', add a step at the steps' indentation: '      - name: Query budget on the fresh database (src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts)', '        if: matrix.shard == 1', '        run: pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mts src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts'. Then change the next step's run line from `pnpm test:int --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/3` to `pnpm test:int --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/3 --exclude src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts`, so the file runs once, before any other file has written to the database. Change nothing else in the job.

commits.title: Query budget: the same counts with 20 stores that have every per-store feature on, and the difference held

changes.how: Test support shared with step 1.12. Export seedStores({ count, pages = 30, products = 200, features }): it makes 'count' open stores named budget-<run>-<n> with makeCapacityStore() of src/server/capacity-test-support.ts, sets setup_completed_at and status active, and gives each store 'pages' published pages and 'products' active products with one variant and one price in the store's first market, by set-based SQL (insert ... select from generate_series), copying the column lists from the demo store's own rows (select one row of commerce.pages and commerce.products of the store 'demo' to see which columns are required). features is 'shop' (stores.features = array['shop']) or 'all'. For 'all' it switches on, with nothing due: the chat agent, the picture model and an AI key of the store's own (a row in the store's AI settings with a dummy encrypted key; use the saver the admin action uses, not raw SQL, so the key is encrypted); open books (the ledger of D478); Tripletex, Fiken and eBay connections marked on with stub tokens (src/server/tripletex-test-support.ts and src/server/fiken-test-support.ts show how tests make them); auto-archive of finished orders; an AI budget; one repeating Work invoice whose next date is 30 days away; two email automations that are on with nobody enrolled; one ad connection; and a support desk with an inbound email address. Export SEEDED_FEATURES: the list of names of what 'all' switches on, which query-budget.int.test.ts prints and asserts is 14 long. Export removeSeed(run) that deletes the stores it made. Each feature's switch is found by reading that feature's admin action under src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/ and calling the server function it calls.

Add a second describe block 'with 20 stores': in beforeAll, seedStores({ count: 19, features: 'all' }) and switch the same features on for the store the first block used, so 20 stores have them; in afterAll, removeSeed. Run parts A to D again and record under queryBudget.twenty. For each name also compute growth = twenty minus one, for statements and for rowsRead, and hold it in queryBudget.growth[<name>]: it may not rise, and it fails when it fell until the baseline is lowered. Add three 'would notice' cases that prove the test sees what the plan names: (1) measure a function that runs one extra select per seeded store beside dispatcher.alt-texts' job and assert its statements are the job's plus 20; (2) measure listPublishedPages(storeId) from src/server/pages.ts against a copy of its query with 'store_id is not distinct from' and assert the copy's rowsRead grows with 20 stores where the function's does not (if step 0.23 has not landed, the function itself still grows: then assert only that growth is recorded for it and leave a comment naming step 0.23); (3) measure runLedgerPosting() from src/server/ledger.ts and assert that its statements with 20 open books are held in queryBudget.twenty, so one more statement per book fails the comparison.
Again by FIRST=1 UPDATE_BASELINE=1 pnpm vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mts src/server/query-budget.int.test.ts: it adds queryBudget.twenty and queryBudget.growth.

do_not: Do not change what a job does, its order in the list or its key: the key is the job's row in commerce.cron_jobs.
Do not add a margin to a count to make a wobbling job pass: a count that changes between runs on the same database is a finding to report.

Do not let a job reach the network: the test database has no provider keys; a job that tries is a failure to report, not something to mock around, unless the job already takes a deps argument (runThemeShots takes a photographer: pass one that throws if called).
Do not count with pg_stat_database's commits, and do not count time.
Do not seed by writing a feature's secret in plain SQL; use the feature's own saver so encrypted columns hold what the app can read.
Do not fix a job that grows with the number of stores here: steps 0.27 to 0.31, 3.2 and 3.6 do that; this step records the growth.
stop_if: countStatements is not exported from src/db/statement-count.ts: step 1.9 is not done.
A job or route launches a browser, calls a provider or throws when there is nothing to do: report its name.
The same job gives different statement counts on three runs in a row.
rowsRead does not settle within 15 seconds or differs by more than 0 between runs: report the job; rows read may then be held for the 20-store run only.
A feature of the list cannot be switched on from a server function without a real provider answer (eBay, an ad platform): leave it out, say which in SEEDED_FEATURES' comment and in your report.
The whole file takes over 5 minutes in pnpm test:int.

The budget file passes on a freshly seeded database but fails in CI's 'Query budget on the fresh database' step with the same commit: report the names and both figures; do not raise a figure or add a margin.
